charon.lon_evidence: ISIS label: PositiveEast, CenterLongitude 0, -180..180; GeoTIFF central_meridian 0
charon.nodata_fill: flat DN 115.0 (mean of the imaged pixels) where New Horizons saw nothing (mostly south of ~30 S): not imaged, not terrain
charon.note: New Horizons LORRI/MVIC global mosaic, 2017 (NASA/JHUAPL/SwRI/LPI, USGS); the south was in darkness

earth.lon_evidence: WebWorldWind BMNGOneImageLayer.js drapes this file on Sector.FULL_SPHERE = (-90, 90, -180, 180)
earth.note: NASA Blue Marble Next Generation, May 2004 (topography and bathymetry shading)

earth_night.lon_evidence: no bounds in the Marble dgml; registered against the Blue Marble (land/ocean base, best shift 0, not mirrored) and city positions in verify_textures_sky.py
earth_night.note: City lights from DMSP-OLS (NASA GSFC / NOAA NGDC), over a dark land and ocean base

jupiter.lon_evidence: annotated original (USGS jupiter_from_cassini.tif) labels 180 ... 0 ... 180 decreasing to the right, i.e. west longitudes: east increases to the right, left edge 180 W; the web copy is the same picture (correlation 0.999 at zero shift, not mirrored); no flip applied. Longitude system not stated in the file (the Great Red Spot drifts, so its position is a Dec 2000 snapshot)
jupiter.note: Cassini ISS colour map PIA07782, Dec 2000 (NASA/JPL/Space Science Institute)

mars.lon_evidence: ISIS label: PositiveEast, planetocentric, CenterLongitude 0, -180..180; GeoTIFF central_meridian 0
mars.note: Viking Orbiter colour mosaic, red and violet filters (NASA, PDS, USGS)

mercury.lon_evidence: ISIS label: PositiveEast, CenterLongitude 0, -180..180; GeoTIFF central_meridian 0
mercury.note: MESSENGER MDIS 750 nm global mosaic, May 2013 (NASA/JHUAPL/ASU, USGS)

moon.lon_evidence: Stellarium sphere-texture convention (prime meridian at the centre); proved by maria and craters (Tycho, Mare Crisium, Mare Humorum) in verify_textures_sky.py
moon.note: LRO LROC WAC Hapke-normalised albedo (Stellarium map by R. Kabatsayev)

pluto.lon_evidence: ISIS label: PositiveEast, CenterLongitude 180, 0..360 (left edge 0 E); GeoTIFF central_meridian 180
pluto.nodata_fill: flat DN 109.0 (mean of the imaged pixels) where New Horizons saw nothing (mostly south of ~30 S, in polar night during the 2015 flyby): not imaged, not terrain
pluto.note: New Horizons LORRI/MVIC global mosaic, 2017 (NASA/JHUAPL/SwRI/LPI, USGS); the south was in darkness

sun.lon_evidence: Stellarium sphere-texture convention (prime meridian at the centre); a generic texture of HMI data from Aug 2025 and Dec 2019 with no Carrington registration
sun.note: SDO HMI continuum (Stellarium map by R. Kabatsayev), coloured by the TSIS-1 spectrum

venus.lon_evidence: ISIS label: PositiveEast, CenterLongitude 0, -180..180; GeoTIFF central_meridian 0
venus.nodata_fill: flat DN 129.0 (mean of the imaged pixels) in Magellan's swath gaps and polar holes
venus.note: Magellan radar (C3-MIDR mosaic, NASA/JPL, USGS) — radar brightness under the clouds, not what an eye sees

colour_method: CIE 1931 2-degree observer (colour-science 0.4.6 table), 1 nm grid 360-830 nm, linear interpolation of each spectrum (Karkoschka air wavelengths; TSIS 1 nm bins at their centres). Planets and Titan: XYZ of albedo x TSIS-1 sunlight, normalised so a perfect white reflector has Y = 1, Bradford-adapted from the Sun's white to D65, IEC 61966-2-1 sRGB matrix and transfer curve, x 255, rounded; srgb_illuminant_E is the same with an equal-energy illuminant, as a cross-check. Sun: XYZ of the TSIS-1 spectrum through the same matrix without adaptation, largest channel scaled to 1. Disk-averaged colours of July 1995 (Uranus changes with season); no limb darkening or banding.

jupiter.spectrum: Karkoschka (1998) 1995LOW.TAB column "JUPITER ALBEDO": full-disk albedo at 6.8 deg phase

neptune.note: Karkoschka 1998: measured disk spectrum (ESO, July 1995) — no real map exists

saturn.note: Karkoschka 1998: measured disk spectrum, ESO 1995 (globe; rings edge-on)
saturn.spectrum: Karkoschka (1998) 1995LOW.TAB column "SATURN ALBEDO": full-disk albedo at 5.7 deg phase, rings edge-on (zero tilt)

sun.note: TSIS-1 solar spectrum (sunlight above the atmosphere)
sun.source: TSIS-1 HSRS v2, Coddington et al. 2023 (LASP), as resampled in OrbitalCommons/starfield
sun.spectrum: TSIS-1 Hybrid Solar Reference Spectrum v2, 1 nm box means (solar irradiance at 1 AU)

titan.note: Karkoschka 1998: measured disk spectrum of the haze, ESO 1995
titan.spectrum: Karkoschka (1998) 1995LOW.TAB column "TITAN ALBEDO": full-disk albedo at 5.7 deg phase

uranus.note: Karkoschka 1998: measured disk spectrum (ESO, July 1995) — no real map exists

convention: Equirectangular; row 0 = +90 deg latitude; longitude east-positive and increasing to the right; column x covers longitudes lon_left_deg + 360 x / width .. + 360 (x + 1) / width.
resampling: USGS GeoTIFFs: exact area average of the source pixels whose centres fall in each output pixel, nodata (0) excluded. Stellarium and Cassini maps: exact 2x2 (Moon, Jupiter) or 8x8 (Sun, in linear light) box average. City lights: PIL BOX filter 2700 -> 2048. Blue Marble: shipped byte for byte. JPEG quality 85 (Pillow 11.3.0).
